answer: Yes. Marguerite has the depth appropriate to a protagonist, moving from sharp criticism toward weary acceptance without losing her wit or humanity. Desmond and Teodor gain individuality through distinctive habits and changing responses: Desmond’s defensive humor develops into practical solidarity, while Teodor’s vocal anxiety becomes quiet resignation. Even the briefly appearing Facilities liaison receives a moment of sympathetic recognition, making her more than a bureaucratic obstacle. The characters’ differing levels of development suit their roles.
